heading: INT. ABANDONED DRIVE-IN PROJECTION BOOTH - DUSK

units.text: INT. ABANDONED DRIVE-IN PROJECTION BOOTH - DUSK
Dust hangs in the last orange light like a held breath.
A cracked projector squats in the middle of the room, and through the small square window the huge blank screen glows pink, empty of everything but weeds at its feet.
ROSALIND "ROZ" BEAUMONT, sixty-eight, runs a thumb along the projector's lens cap as if checking a sleeping animal for a pulse.
Her grandson, KWAME ASANTE-BEAUMONT, fifteen, stands in the doorway with a duffel bag he has not put down.
Mum said you'd be mad.
units.name: KWAME

units.text: Your mother's been saying that since 1994. I've never once been mad on schedule.
units.name: ROZ

units.text: He lets the bag slide to the floor.
She does not turn around.
You want to see something?
units.name: ROZ

units.text: She flips a rusted switch.
Nothing.
She flips it again.
The projector coughs, and a long, trembling beam of white light leaps out the window and lands on the screen like a thrown door.
It works?
units.name: KWAME

units.text: It does not. That's the sun, in the glass. Always happens at dusk.
units.name: ROZ

units.text: They both watch the shape of the light slide down the screen and fade.
I'm sorry about Grandad.
units.name: KWAME

units.text: Mm.
units.name: ROZ

units.text: I'm sorry I didn't come.
units.name: KWAME

units.text: Sit down, you're blocking my view.
units.name: ROZ

units.text: He sits.
She finally turns, and puts a hand briefly on his hair.
